pages.observed: Five samples 0.0 to 0.8 s of an airport curb scene in flat vector style: phone with route map and Ride requested card over a pickup area, airport sign, bench, suitcase, skyline, white generic car at left edge. Caption begins at 0.6 s. Lower third of frame is empty dark asphalt.

Samples 1.0 to 1.8 s. The white generic car slides right along the curb, red brake lamp on from 1.2 s, and nears the bay box. Phone card still reads Ride requested. Lower third of the frame is empty dark asphalt, caption sits mid-lower.

Exterior car stops at bay at 2.0 to 2.2 s, then cut at 2.4 s to the cab interior: dark dashboard, wheel tilted, two empty seat headrests, windshield showing the airport sign. The exterior phone card remains floating over the interior view at left. Texas outline card at top right.

Interior view held 3.0 to 3.8 s. The wheel rotates by itself with the seats empty while the windshield scenery slides. The exterior phone card still hovers over the interior and still says Ride requested. Lower third is empty seat backs.

Interior shot holds 4.0 to 4.6 s with little change. At 4.8 s a cut returns to the exterior curb: big tilted phone showing Ride requested in foreground, car parked in bay at right, Texas locator dot appears in the card. Caption absent at 4.8 s.

Samples 5.0 to 5.8 s. Foreground phone covers the rear half of the car. At 5.6 s the card text flips to Arriving At the curb and the car pin slides to the destination pin by 5.8 s. Locator card shows a dot then a ring on Texas. Caption reads the airport included.

Curb scene holds nearly still 6.0 to 6.6 s with Arriving on the phone and no caption from 6.2 s. At 6.8 s cut to a tabletop view with a pale paper map with three pins and a February page on a calendar stand, plain sky and brown table.

Table with pale map, February page and three small pins. Map static 7.0 to 7.4 s, then blue river strokes and tan streets draw in from 7.6 s. Caption reads The service began in February. Lower half of frame is empty wood table.

Map draws: two blue river lines grow downward, a tan ring road and diagonal roads appear around the pins. Texas locator card fades away by 8.2 s. Caption unchanged. Lower half of frame remains empty wood.

Map enlarges at 9.2 s. The 60 square miles Limited area tag appears at 9.4 s, a February page crosses the map and lands lower left by 9.8 s, and a black outline starts to draw beside the tag. Caption changes at 9.4 s to in a limited area of sixty square miles.

A black line draws around the pin cluster over 10.0 to 10.6 s and closes into a shaded polygon at 10.8 s. No car appears on this map, the pins are small circle marks. Lower half of the frame is empty wood table.
Held frame for the whole 1.0 s span 11.0 to 11.8 s. The closed polygon, tag and calendar are unchanged from one sample to the next. Lower third is empty table.

Map held to 12.2 s with no caption between 11.8 and 12.8 s except at 12.8 s. At 12.4 s hard cut to a top-down view of the white car sitting on brown water with cream ledges, green bank and bushes. Disclosure changes to A different car, April 20th account. Car does not move 12.4 to 12.8 s. Caption appears at 12.8 s.

Five samples 13.0 to 13.8 s show the same composition. The car, its roof pod, the ledges and bushes do not move between samples, only a slight shimmer in the water. The car sits on a pale bank strip rather than in the brown current. Caption holds.

From 14.0 s the car begins to drift sideways and slightly rotate on the pale shelf next to the water, then at 14.8 s the camera has moved and the car sits lower right. The car stays on pale ledge strips and never visibly sinks or leaves the bank in these samples.

The car is clearly carried: it slews and slides leftward and enlarges toward the camera over 15.0 to 15.8 s, with foam and wake lines on the brown water and a soft shadow. This is the readable swept-away passage.
Car exits left by 16.4 s. At 16.6 and 16.8 s the frame shows only empty brown creek, banks and bushes with the caption removed. The scene ends on an empty creek with the car out of frame.

The empty creek frame holds 16.6 to 17.2 s with no subject. At 17.4 s cut to a flooded street, white car already in water to the wheel arches. Foreground pavement fills the lower 40 percent. Caption starts at 17.6 s.

The car settles lower in the water over the five samples, wheels disappearing under brown water and its reflection dimming. Camera static. Pavement in lower 40 percent of frame is empty. No hazard lamps visible yet.

Hazard lamps blink amber from 19.2 s on the small stopped car. At 19.8 s the view jumps to a close side view of the car sunk to the doors in water with defocused houses behind. Empty cabin windows visible. Foreground pavement below.

Held close view of the stranded car with blinking amber lamps and an empty cabin with visible headrests. Only the lamps and slight ripples change across 20.0 to 20.8 s. Lower 40 percent of frame is blank pavement.
Same held close shot as the previous page. Only the lamp blink changes. Caption leaves at 21.4 s, leaving 0.4 s with no caption. Roughly 40 percent of the frame below the water is empty pavement.

At 22.2 s cut to a plain olive wall and brown desk with a tilted cream card titled Federal recall record, subtitle Vehicle safety recall, a ruled line and a pen at the right edge. The card is partly cropped at the right. Rows are still empty at 22.8 s with only a cursor tick. No car icons yet.

Card settles on the desk as rows type in. By 23.8 s it reads Recall type Software and Potential units affected 3,791. Top 35 percent of the frame is plain olive wall and the bottom 20 percent is plain wall. The card's text is small at phone width.

Card holds unchanged 24.0 to 24.6 s under the caption Waymo filed a software recall. At 24.8 s the view moves and a 10 by 5 dashed grid appears with two small white car icons filled at upper left, caption changes to that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.

Grid fills with icons through 25.8 s while a hand with a wooden stamp slides in from the right and across the card. A human hand and forearm appears here for the first time in the film. The stamp has no visible mark yet.

The stamp lands crooked leaving an orange Software recall mark and a tag reading Nearly 3,800 vehicles 3,791 potentially affected in the record drops over the grid at 26.2 s. Grid is full. Stamp mark is small at phone width. Lower 20 percent is plain wall.
Stamp mark remains, hand gone by 27.4 s. Composition then holds static for about 0.6 s to 27.8 s with no caption from 27.6 s. Bottom third of frame is empty wall.

Desk cut to a road scene at 28.2 s. Car enters at left, quote card with the recall sentence fades in from 28.6 s. No standing water is visible on the road at this point, only a small wake line under the wheels. Lower 45 percent is grass and caption.

The car cruises with scrolling background and lane marks at constant pace. It is small, about 20 percent of the frame height, with no standing water visible on the roadway ahead and no brake lamp lit. Quote card static top left. Bottom 40 percent is grass and caption.

Brake lamp turns red at 30.0 s and a grey oval of standing water drifts in from the right. The car remains in the same screen position and small in frame. Captioned clause is the car slowing, which the brake lamp and approaching water show.

Wide car slowing 31.0 to 31.4 s then a cut to a close side view at 31.6 s. The wake line under the close car is drawn as wavy white lines on dark asphalt. The grey puddle shows at the right edge at 31.8 s. The car has not yet entered the water.

Close car holds screen position while a puddle edge slides in from the right and reaches the nose at 32.8 s. May is highlighted at 32.8 s. The car has not entered the water yet at 32.8 s. Lower 40 percent is grass and caption.

The car's front wheel enters the grey water with ripples and wake streaks from 33.4 s, and the word may glows orange. The car's screen position barely changes while the road and water slide under it. This is the signature roll-in.

Car continues forward through the grey water with a wake and spray at the wheel, no stop drawn, the highlighted may stays. This passage is readable at phone size as a car driving into a puddle. Bottom 40 percent is grass and caption.

Water roll-in continues to 35.4 s, then a cut to the recall card enlarged. The card's lower half is blank cream paper where the remedy row is expected, not yet written. No remedy row appears by 35.8 s.

The remedy row writes in as a peach highlighted block by 36.4 s reading The remedy is currently under development. A hand holding a pen arrives from the right by 36.6 to 36.8 s. Card text is moderately legible at phone width. Lower third is empty wall.

A pen tip rests near the remedy text for 37.0 to 37.6 s with minimal movement, then at 37.8 s a stamp and second forearm come in from the lower right. Remedy text is clearly readable at 390 px width. Lower third empty wall.

The stamp hand sits over the lower left of the card for 38.0 to 38.6 s with small motion. The orange Under development mark only starts to appear at 38.8 s and is largely hidden behind the stamp. Two forearms occupy the right side of the card. Lower third is empty wall.

The orange Under development stamp is fully visible by 39.0 s and the hands exit right. Card with remedy row and stamp holds, readable at phone size. Caption leaves at 39.4 s, bottom third is empty wall.

New scene at 40.0 s with four white cars receding in a row, a small Vehicle maps card and April calendar page at upper right. Static for about 0.4 s, then a Weather limits tightened tag slides in from the left at 40.4 s. Lower third is wet asphalt with reflections.

Only the weather tag moves, drifting rightward over 0.8 s. The four cars do not move or change, no check marks yet. Calendar page still reads April with blank lines. Lower 40 percent of frame is wet asphalt.

Held scene with only a slight tag sway across the five samples. No checkmarks, no calendar change. Same caption as the previous page. About 2.8 s of this row-of-cars composition has now passed with one tag move. Lower 40 percent is empty wet asphalt.

Held 43.0 to 43.4 s with no change, then at 43.6 s a cut to a closer, lower angle on the same car row. The calendar page still shows April with blank lines and no day number, and no check marks have appeared on any car yet.

Check marks appear over each car in sequence, which depicts every car receiving the update. The April calendar page still shows only the word April with grey placeholder lines and no 20 visible in these samples. Vehicle maps card gets a small circle at 44.8 s.

All visible car badges show check marks and the Vehicle maps card shows updated with a check at 45.2 s. The April page still shows only April with blank grey lines, no numeral 20. The frame holds unchanged 45.4 to 45.8 s. Lower 40 percent is wet asphalt.

The calendar flips at 46.4 s to a bold 20 under April while the caption says April twentieth. Checks on all four cars remain. The 20 is legible at phone width though small relative to the frame. Bottom 40 percent is wet asphalt.

The checked row holds static 47.0 to 47.6 s. At 47.8 s cut to the airport curb with a new disclosure A generic airport ride, not the flood cars. The car is parked small in the bay and the phone card says Arriving At the curb. No caption yet.

Car waits at the bay and from 48.6 s its rear door swings open, showing a dark gap, while the caption says So the airport ride is open. The car is small at about a quarter of frame width. The lower 40 percent of frame is empty asphalt.
Rear door stays open and the car holds still for the whole 49.0 to 49.8 s span. Nothing else moves. The frame ends with no caption at 49.8 s. Lower 40 percent is empty asphalt.

At 50.0 s the camera reframes lower so the car and its open door sit in the upper third with a recall card lying in the road below it showing the remedy row and stamp. The card text is small at phone width. Lower half of frame is blank asphalt.

Recall card slowly enlarges and settles in front of the car, remedy text readable at phone width from 51.2 s. The car and open door stay the same. Nothing else moves. Lower 40 percent is empty asphalt.
The split composition of curb ride plus recall card holds without any motion for the entire 52.0 to 52.8 s span. This is the closing hold. Lower 40 percent of the frame is empty asphalt.

A split-screen: top half the airport curb with car and open door, bottom half the recall card with a small phone beside it. The only motion is an underline tracing under the remedy text over 53.0 to 53.8 s. Lower 40 percent of frame is empty brown desk.

Closing hold with nothing moving for 54.0 to 54.8 s and no caption from 54.2 s. The final answer composition is visible: open car door above and remedy row under development below. Lower 40 percent of frame is empty brown desk.
Fully static hold across 55.0 to 55.8 s with no caption and no camera or object movement. About 1.9 s of unchanging frame has now run since 53.8 s. Bottom 40 percent of the frame is empty brown desk.

Credits card with the Texas flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, URL and source lines appears at 56.0 s and is static from 56.2 s. Credit text is small, readable at native size, small at phone width. Bottom 40 percent of card is empty dark.
Static credits card, identical across all five samples. Lower 40 percent of the card is empty dark. Credit text is small at phone width.
Identical static credits card across the five samples 58.0 to 58.8 s. No motion, no audio info in the image. Lower 40 percent is empty dark.
Identical static credits card across 59.0 to 59.8 s. No motion. Lower 40 percent is empty dark.
Identical static credits card across 60.0 to 60.8 s. No motion. Lower 40 percent is empty dark.
Final frame is the same credits card, no fade out. The film ends on the held credits at 60.967 s.
